If there's any one place where the galaxy's trash finally comes to rest, it's Lotho.''"
"''Sounds like you kind of ''love it'', Han.''"
"''Find me a smuggler who doesn't.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]|[[Star Wars (2013) 19|''Star Wars'' (2013) 19]]}} '''Lotho Minor''', also known as the '''Junk World''' or simply '''Lotho''', was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] that was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Junker/Legends|Junker]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. Used as a dumping ground, its surface was covered with junk and trash amassed over a number of generations, which brought salvage operations to the planet to find junk that could still be used. Following [[Gender/Legends|his]] defeat during the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]], the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] went into exile in the bowels of Lotho Minor, where he lost his mind until he was found by his brother, [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]], over a [[Standard decade/Legends|decade]] later. ==Description== [[File:LothoMinorJunk-TCW.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The junk fields of Lotho Minor]] {{Quote|The cargo you just dropped off. What planet did it come from?''"
"''The junk fields, on planet Lotho Minor.|[[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]] and a [[Unidentified Sakiyan cargo hauler/Legends|cargo hauler]]|audio=Lotho_Minor_1.flac|}} Lotho Minor, also known simply as Lotho, was located in the [[Lotho Minor system/Legends|Lotho Minor system]], within the [[Wazta sector/Legends|Wazta sector]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. A terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]], its surface was covered with refuse, piled over countless generations so that enormous heaps of trash stood as tall as [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]]. The gutted and rotting hulls of ancient [[Starship/Legends|starships]] poked through the more recent garbage, giving the landscape the eerie feel of an industrial graveyard. Huge pools of toxic sludge and the periodic bursts of [[Acid rain/Legends|acid rain]] made its ruined ecosystem one of the most dangerous in the galaxy. The planet's [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] was breathable, though hot and caustic, while foul-smelling fog limited visibility. ==History== {{Quote|This is where you live? How long have you been here?''"
"''Years and years and years.|Savage Opress and Darth Maul|audio=Lotho_Minor_3.flac|}} For [[Time/Legends|time]] immemorial, Lotho Minor was an industrial dumping ground for neighboring worlds. Cargo ships routinely dropped holds of refuse onto the planet, caring little as to what would become of it. Long ago, immense [[Fire-breather/Legends|refuse incinerator droids]] were programmed to incinerate Lotho Minor's garbage.{{SWE|technology|firebreather|fire-breather}} By the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],{{FactFile2014|24|MAU 1-2|Darth Maul's Cybernetic Legs}} they continued to labor amid the mountains of refuse; those unfortunate to live on Lotho Minor did not know the [[Droid/Legends|droids']] origins and referred to them simply as "[[Fire/Legends|fire]]-breathers." Salvage operations also dug through the planet-wide junkyard, looking to reclaim and recondition reusable or obsolete machinery, and Lotho Minor came to also be known as the Junk World. In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' establishes that the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] happens in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. the shattered body of [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], a [[Dathomirian/Legends|Dathomirian]] [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]], was dumped amid Lotho Minor's refuse after [[Gender/Legends|his]] defeat at the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]].''[[The Clone Wars: The Sith Hunters]]'' His driving desire to cling to life pushed him to rebuild himself, living in hiding in the [[Cave/Legends|caves]] beneath Lotho Minor's surface and subsisting off garbage and vermin for over a [[Standard decade/Legends|decade]]. An [[Anacondan/Legends|Anacondan]] known as [[Morley/Legends|Morley]] pledged loyalty to Maul to survive, promising to lure unwitting prey into Maul's hungry clutches. Lotho Minor was neutral during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. In 20 BBY, [[Mother (title)/Legends|Mother]] [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]] of the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]] tasked [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]] with finding Maul, his long lost brother. A [[Talisman of Finding/Legends|mystical talisman]] pointed him in the direction of Lotho Minor; while [[Mission to Lotho Minor/Legends|scouring]] the planet's endless wastes for his brother,{{SWE|groups|junkers|Junkers}} Opress encountered Morley, who guided him past such threats as the enormous fire-breathers and a tribe of territorial [[Junker/Legends|Junkers]]. He lured Opress into a [[Darth Maul's lair/Legends|cave]], where Maul was said to live. There, Opress found his brother, though his mind was shattered. He brought Maul back to [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]], where Talzin restored his body and mind.{{TCW|Revenge (episode)}} [[File:Junkers.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A pair of Junkers on Lotho Minor]] By [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], Lotho Minor had come to attract all sorts of nefarious types, including [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]]. [[Seren Song]], a [[Spy/Legends|spy]] for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] took refuge from the infamous droid [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[IG-88 assassin droid/Legends|IG-88]] in the planet's junk fields. When she tried escaping aboard her [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL Y-wing starfighter]], the droid tagged it with a [[Homing beacon/Legends|homing beacon]] and pursued in its [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]], the [[IG-2000/Legends|''IG-2000'']]. When the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] arrived in the Lotho Minor system to [[Mission to Lotho Minor (Galactic Civil War)|investigate]] Song's distress call, it was engaged by IG-88 before escaping into [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. ==Inhabitants== {{Quote|Trust me, not everything on this planet is junk.…There are things like me, things that live and breathe.|Morley|audio=Lotho_Minor_4.flac|}} Lotho Minor was apparently the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the Junkers [[Species/Legends|species]]. Living in tribes, the mysterious Junkers appeared to be a strange hybrid of organic life and mechanical debris, and no one was quite sure of their origin. Lotho Minor's role as a galactic dumping ground did not encouraged any deep exploration of Junker culture or biology, nor did their violent territoriality. The Junkers lived off the scrap found on their homeworld's surface, augmenting their strange and twisted bodies with [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic]] enhancements. They lived on Lotho Minor for so long that it was impossible to tell where their bodies ended and where the refuse began. ==Behind the scenes== [[File:Lotho_Minor_Spirit_Of_A.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Lotho Minor environment design illustration by Kilian Plunkett]] Lotho Minor was originally created for "[[Brothers (episode)|Brothers]]," the twenty-first episode of the animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''{{'}} [[The Clone Wars: Season Four|fourth season]], which originally aired [[March 9]], [[2012]].''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Episode Guide]]'' Several "spirit of" designs for Lotho Minor were illustrated by [[Kilian Plunkett]] and [[Pat Presley]]. It was referred to as Lamoth in some pieces of concept art.{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/brothers-concept-art-gallery|text="Brothers" Concept Art Gallery}} {{C|Slides 5, 6, 9, and 10}} Lotho Minor later reappeared in [[Star Wars (2013) 19|''Star Wars'' (2013) 19]], which was written by [[Brian Wood]] and illustrated by [[Carlos D'Anda]]. The nineteenth issue of [[Dark Horse Comics]]' [[Star Wars (2013)|''Star Wars'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series, it was released on [[July 9]],
